full_judgment: 13. We have already pointed out that undisputedly the suit land was recorded in the name of the deity in the CS Khatian Exhibits 1 and 1(a). The CS Khatian has a presumption of correctness under section 103(B) of the Bengal Tenancy Act but the SA Khatian has no such presumptive value, it is true that presumption of correctness of entry in the CS Khatian is rebuttable by adducing cogent and reliable evidence, in the instant case there is no attempt even to rebut the correctness of entry ill the CS Khatian prepared in the name of the deity. The High Court Division relying on the case of Sukumar Bose and others vs Abani Kumar Halder and others reported in 60 CWN 778 observed that in that case it was held that a debuttor property can never be turned into a secular property, in view of the proposition that once a property becomes a property of the deity which is immortal, it continues to be a property of the deity for all times to come. The dedication of the property to an idol may take place at the time of installation of the idol or may precede it or it may take place after the installation of the deity and after the dedication in all cases it remains the property of the idol and ceases to be the property of the donor. Even if a particular image may be destroyed, the deity whose visible form the image continues for ever and its property as debuttor property remains totally unaffected.
